source.title: Interpreting Neural Networks through the Polytope Lens
source.authors: Sid Black; Lee D. Sharkey; Léo Grinsztajn; Eric Winsor; Daniel A. Braun; Jacob Merizian; Kip Parker; Carlos Ram'on Guevara; Beren Millidge; Gabriel Alfour; Connor Leahy

record.tranche_reason: The paper argues that neuron- and direction-based interpretations need qualification because semantics can depend on activation regions, and reports results on monosemantic clusters and directions. It does not directly test the listed versions about individual neurons.
record.gate_note: The InceptionV1 neuron example and GPT2-Medium neuron example in the introduction are cited illustrations, not results from this study, so they are not recorded as rows. The study's own results below concern clusters and directions, rather than individual-neuron polysemanticity.
record.test_reason: The study is mainly about polytopes, but it does report its own neuron-level observations. It states that basis directions (individual neurons) in GPT2-small and InceptionV1 'still appear highly polysemantic'. Figures 1–2 give the authors' own examples: a polysemantic neuron in PyTorch InceptionV1 (with batch norm) and one in GPT2-Medium. This is weak, qualitative evidence bearing on V1 and V2. The cluster and NMF-direction results concern other units and do not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also state that evidence supports predictions 1 (polysemantic directions overlap monosemantic regions) and 2 (polytope boundaries reflect semantic boundaries), and only partially supports prediction 3 (polytopes mark the on/off-distribution of directions). They say they are unsure the costs of the polytope lens are worth the gains.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce or apply the original sources' methods for identifying polysemantic neurons.
record.method_sensitivity: The analysis distinguishes activation clusters, spline-code clusters, NMF directions, and basis directions; the reported semantic coherence differs across these representations.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation and spline-code clusters, and NMF directions, were mostly monosemantic in both models, while basis directions were polysemantic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local activation regions and some non-basis directions are monosemantic even where neurons are polysemantic.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling activations changes class predictions; polytope boundary density is higher between than within classes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Direction semantics depend on activation scale and region.

record.problems: The semantic-coherence findings are qualitative, with no reported proportion of clusters or directions classified as monosemantic. Cluster examples are selected illustrations. The paper says transformer polytopes are an open extension question; its GPT2 analyses use activation and spline-code clustering rather than a direct measurement of neuron polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: Polytope-density and activation-scaling results are not included because they measure class changes and boundary density, not polysemanticity or semantic coherence of neurons, directions, or clusters.

untested.parts: The share of polysemantic MLP neurons and how it varies by layer; only one example neuron and a qualitative remark are given.
Superposition is discussed as a possible cause but not tested.
Not tested; batch norm in the PyTorch InceptionV1 is noted but not compared.
Canonical neurons are not re-examined with better tools.
Scale- and region-dependence is argued for directions, not for neuron polysemanticity labels.

missing.what: Authors' own polysemantic neuron example in PyTorch InceptionV1 (inception5a neuron 233: dog noses, metal poles, maybe boats)
Authors' own polysemantic neuron example in GPT2-Medium (commas in lists, diminutive adjectives, prepositions)

record.verdict_notes: The record wrongly treats Figures 1–2 as cited illustrations; they appear to be the authors' own examples, given the footnote on the PyTorch InceptionV1 implementation. All neuron-level evidence is anecdotal and qualitative, so the V1 and V2 support is weak.

versions.untested_parts: Whether individual neurons in image classifiers respond to multiple unrelated inputs.
The share of MLP neurons in transformer language models responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, and how it varies by layer.
Whether superposition caused the reported polysemanticity.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure due to initialization, regularization, or training noise.
Whether architecture, activation function, or regularization changes the share of polysemantic neurons, or whether that share can be lowered without substantial performance loss.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons, examined with better tools, detect one shared feature or related jobs.
Whether neuron polysemanticity depends on the activation range examined or on how explanations are scored.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Clustered channel activations with HDBSCAN and assessed the semantics of the resulting clusters.
rows.value: The majority of clusters found were monosemantic; examples included clusters corresponding to specific animal types.
rows.note: Qualitative cluster result; this measures activation clusters, not individual neurons.
rows.check: Concerns activation clusters, not neurons; no version applies.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Clustered MLP-layer activations with HDBSCAN and inspected examples from the clusters.

conditions.value: random sample of The Pile test set

rows.value: The majority of clusters found were monosemantic; examples included token-specific and semantic clusters.
rows.note: Qualitative result. The paper notes that higher-level semantic clusters tend to occur later, but does not report a numerical share by layer.

rows.subject: GPT2-small

rows.value: The majority of clusters found were monosemantic; examples included clusters related to detokenization and groups of patients in medical trials.

relation.reason: Figs 1-2 are the authors' own examples, not cited ones (the cited Olah image is Fig. 22). The Sec. 2.1.1 remark is their own observation. So the study's own results bear on V1 and V2, though only qualitatively.

tranche.reason: The authors report their own observations in new settings: a polysemantic neuron in PyTorch InceptionV1 with batch norm (Fig. 1), a GPT2-Medium neuron (Fig. 2), and the Sec. 2.1.1 remark that basis directions in GPT2-small and InceptionV1 look highly polysemantic. These bear on the existence parts of V1 and V2. The evidence is weak and anecdotal. It is not T5, because nothing argues that a version is wrong.

source_check.notes: The polysemanticity evidence is two illustrative neurons (Figs 1-2) and one qualitative sentence (Sec. 2.1.1), with no data, rate or layer breakdown. The study's controls (untrained network) and CIs apply only to its polytope-density experiments. The related-work line that monosemantic neurons seem less common in LMs is a literature remark, not the authors' own result.

statements.correction: Text: basis directions 'still appear highly polysemantic' (Sec. 2.1.1), with no data shown. The untrained-network control and the 99% bootstrapped CIs / SEM apply only to the polytope-density results (Figs 18-19, Apps A-B). Fig. 1 (inception5a/233) and the Sec. 2.1.1 remark have no control and no uncertainty.
statements.problem: The 'why' gives this study controls y and uncertainty y without saying these cover only the polytope-density experiments. The cited neuron evidence has neither. The quote is also altered: the text says 'still appear', not 'still appeared'.
Calling this study qualitative with no share is right.

The statement says nothing about this study beyond citing r7, and the citation fits. Sec. 2.1.1 contrasts NMF directions that look largely monosemantic with basis directions that look highly polysemantic (GPT2-small layer 4, and InceptionV1 by the same procedure). The contrast is qualitative only.
Listing the study as other-group, qualitative InceptionV1 evidence is right. Its authors (Conjecture) share none with the original.

statements.correction: 2211.12312's untrained-network control and 99% bootstrapped CIs cover only the InceptionV1 polytope-density experiments. The GPT2-small remark (Sec. 2.1.1, layer 4 MLP) and the Fig. 2 GPT2-Medium neuron are single qualitative observations with no control and no uncertainty.
statements.problem: The 'why' gives 2211.12312 controls y and uncertainty y with no qualifier, unlike the qualifier it gives 2410.16443. The cited GPT-2 neuron evidence has neither. The 'what' part is accurate.
